symbols.name: input record
symbols.meaning: The first of the two input records, a polynomial in y of degree less than r with complex coefficients.
symbols.quote: Let $\varphi$ and $\psi$ be the two input records, polynomials in $y$ of degree less than $r$ with complex coefficients.

symbols.name: input record
symbols.meaning: The second of the two input records, a polynomial in y of degree less than r with complex coefficients.
symbols.quote: Let $\varphi$ and $\psi$ be the two input records, polynomials in $y$ of degree less than $r$ with complex coefficients.

symbols.name: forward transform
symbols.meaning: The forward transform along the remaining axes, normalized by 1/t on each axis of length t.
symbols.quote: Let $\Theta$ be the forward transform along the remaining axes, normalized by $1/t$ on each axis of length $t$, and let $\Theta^{+}$ be its opposite, which uses the inverse roots of unity.

symbols.name: opposite transform
symbols.meaning: The opposite transform along the remaining axes, which uses the inverse roots of unity in place of those of the forward transform.
symbols.quote: Let $\Theta$ be the forward transform along the remaining axes, normalized by $1/t$ on each axis of length $t$, and let $\Theta^{+}$ be its opposite, which uses the inverse roots of unity.

symbols.name: record count
symbols.meaning: The number of records in the array along the remaining axes, which counts the product of the remaining axis lengths.
symbols.quote: Let $\nu$ be the number of records in the array, the product of the remaining axis lengths.

symbols.name: normalized convolution
symbols.meaning: The normalized convolution of two arrays of records, the cyclic convolution divided by r times the record count.
symbols.quote: Write $\ast$ for cyclic convolution over the remaining axes, $\varphi\star\psi=\varphi\ast\psi/(r\nu)$ for the normalized convolution, and $\odot$ for the product $uv/r$ taken entry by entry.

symbols.name: normalized entrywise product
symbols.meaning: The product of two records divided by r, taken entry by entry on two arrays.
symbols.quote: Write $\ast$ for cyclic convolution over the remaining axes, $\varphi\star\psi=\varphi\ast\psi/(r\nu)$ for the normalized convolution, and $\odot$ for the product $uv/r$ taken entry by entry.

symbols.name: real integer part
symbols.meaning: The integer polynomial whose coefficients, after scaling by 2^p, give the real part of the input record varphi.
symbols.quote: Hence $\varphi=2^{-p}(\varphi_1+i\varphi_2)$ and $\psi=2^{-p}(\psi_1+i\psi_2)$, where $\varphi_1,\varphi_2,\psi_1,\psi_2$ are the real and imaginary integer polynomials, of degree less than $r$, with coefficients bounded by $2^p$.

symbols.name: imaginary integer part
symbols.meaning: The integer polynomial whose coefficients, after scaling by 2^p, give the imaginary part of the input record varphi.
symbols.quote: Hence $\varphi=2^{-p}(\varphi_1+i\varphi_2)$ and $\psi=2^{-p}(\psi_1+i\psi_2)$, where $\varphi_1,\varphi_2,\psi_1,\psi_2$ are the real and imaginary integer polynomials, of degree less than $r$, with coefficients bounded by $2^p$.

symbols.name: real integer part
symbols.meaning: The integer polynomial whose coefficients, after scaling by 2^p, give the real part of the input record psi.
symbols.quote: Hence $\varphi=2^{-p}(\varphi_1+i\varphi_2)$ and $\psi=2^{-p}(\psi_1+i\psi_2)$, where $\varphi_1,\varphi_2,\psi_1,\psi_2$ are the real and imaginary integer polynomials, of degree less than $r$, with coefficients bounded by $2^p$.

symbols.name: imaginary integer part
symbols.meaning: The integer polynomial whose coefficients, after scaling by 2^p, give the imaginary part of the input record psi.
symbols.quote: Hence $\varphi=2^{-p}(\varphi_1+i\varphi_2)$ and $\psi=2^{-p}(\psi_1+i\psi_2)$, where $\varphi_1,\varphi_2,\psi_1,\psi_2$ are the real and imaginary integer polynomials, of degree less than $r$, with coefficients bounded by $2^p$.

symbols.name: storage map
symbols.meaning: The fixed map sending each frequency address to the position where both forward transforms store that frequency.
symbols.quote: Both store frequency $j$ at the position $\mathcal P(j)$ of one fixed map $\mathcal P$.

symbols.name: position index
symbols.meaning: A frequency address of a transform entry, or a coefficient position in the reduction step, a nonnegative integer index.
symbols.quote: The sum $\sum_{k=0}^{t-1}\omega_t^{jk}$, for a frequency address $j$ (an integer index of a transform entry), is $t$ when $t$ divides $j$.

symbols.name: wrap exponent
symbols.meaning: An integer exponent of y, which may be at least r, so that y^e wraps around with a sign flip.
symbols.quote: So $y^e=-y^{e-r}$ for an integer exponent $e\ge r$.

relations.quote: Convolution over the polynomial ring is computed along the [remaining axes](transform-axis.md) as a normalized cyclic convolution of two arrays of records.
Convolution over the polynomial ring takes its products in the [polynomial ring modulo $y^r + 1$](polynomial-ring-mod-yr-plus-1.md), $R_r$, where $y^r=-1$.
Convolution over the polynomial ring computes its transforms by [synthetic polynomial transforms](synthetic-transforms.md), whose roots of unity are powers of $y$.
Convolution over the polynomial ring computes its record products by [signed coefficient packing](signed-packing.md), which turns each polynomial product into an integer product.
Convolution over the polynomial ring reads each coefficient as the [centered residue](centered-residue.md) modulo $B$ of the value left after the lower blocks are removed.
Convolution over the polynomial ring extracts its blocks by a [carry scan](carry-propagation.md): it takes each centered residue, subtracts it, and divides by $B$.
